title: Altera, OQC, and NVIDIA Demonstrate Direct-RF FPGA Quantum System Controller Reference Design at SC26 - Quantum Computing Report
author: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
text:
Altera Corporation, in collaboration with Oxford Quantum Circuits (OQC) and NVIDIA, has unveiled an end-to-end quantum system controller reference design built on an Altera Agilex 9 Direct RF FPGA. Demonstrated live at the SC26 supercomputing conference in Chicago, the architecture links real-time FPGA control and readout electronics with a next-generation OQC superconducting processor and NVIDIA GPUs over NVIDIA NVQLink.

Conventional superconducting quantum control stacks require multi-chassis racks of discrete digital-to-analog converters, analog mixers, and local oscillators that scale poorly with qubit count. By integrating direct-RF data converters and multi-channel frequency multiplexing onto a single programmable device, the Agilex 9 Direct RF FPGA performs pulse synthesis, synchronized scheduling, qubit initialization, and resonator spectroscopy through OQC’s RF conditioning hardware without external analog conversion stages.

Across the NVQLink interconnect, CUDA-driven GPU kernels offload compute-intensive calibration workflows and machine-learning readout classification from the real-time control loop. The software package also includes a built-in controller emulation path so developers can validate firmware and hybrid algorithms prior to physical QPU deployment, with general release scheduled for January 2027.

Read Altera’s official announcement here. Related QCR coverage of NVQLink control architectures includes Quandela’s live photonic FPGA-to-GPU integration here, NVIDIA’s CUDA-Q Logical ecosystem integrations here, and our SC26 report on NVIDIA’s CUDA-Q QEC 0.9.0 and Slurm 26.11 releases here.
